title: The Leeds office
text: Dear all, by now you will have heard the rumours, so here is the truth. The Leeds office is being made {{redundant|redundant}} at the end of March, and I am not {{at liberty|at liberty}} to share the figures behind that decision yet. It {{irritates|irritate}} me to break news like this by email, but HR insists on a paper trail. Every affected colleague will get a one-to-one with me next week. I want this to stay {{amicable|amicable}}, whatever the unions decide to do.

title: Gran's flat
text:
Mum: Did you get to Gran's today?
Sam: Yeah. She looked so {{frail|frail}}, Mum. She needed both hands on the kettle.
Mum: She's eighty-nine, love. Was the flat {{damp|damp}} again?
Sam: Worse. Black patches on the bedroom wall. The landlord gave some {{feeble|feeble}} excuse about the gutters.
Mum: Don't start, {{petal|petal}}. I'll ring him on Monday and I won't be polite.

title: Below the ridge
text: Below the ridge, a {{diminutive|diminutive}} fox waits in the {{dense|dense}} bracken. It is a hunter by instinct and a {{scavenger|scavenger}} by necessity, because the winter here is long and prey is scarce. A red kite has already found the {{carrion|carrion}} of a sheep that fell in the night. The fox will have to wait its turn, and it knows it.

title: Two brothers and a will
text: Her third film {{obliterates|obliterate}} any doubt that she can direct actors. Two brothers return to a farmhouse in Cumbria to settle their mother's will, and an old {{enmity|enmity}} wakes up with them. The only warmth comes from an {{amiable|amiable}} vicar who keeps turning up with casseroles nobody asked for. If anything {{dampens|dampen}} the film, it is the score, which tells you what to feel ten seconds before the actors do. Four stars.

title: Question seven
text:
"Question seven. Which Latin word meaning 'at the back' is also a polite way of saying your bottom?"
"{{Posterior|posterior}}!" shouted Dave, before the host had finished.
"Thank you, Dave. Three pints in and he has no {{inhibitions|inhibition}} left at all."
"It's a {{specimen|specimen}} of a quiz, this," Dave said, pleased with himself, and nobody had the heart to tell him that wasn't quite how the word worked.

title: The jar from Dorset
text: The {{specimen|specimen}} arrived from Dorset in a jar of cloudy spirit, a {{diminutive|diminutive}} beetle no bigger than a grain of rice. Marcus wiped the bench with a {{damp|damp}} cloth, laid out every {{utensil|utensil}} he owned, and then sat looking at it for twenty minutes without touching anything. "It's the first one found in Britain since 1911," he said. "I'm not going to rush it."

title: The drawer of shame
text: Every kitchen has one drawer that will not close. Mine holds at least one {{redundant|redundant}} {{utensil|utensil}} for every job: three peelers, a {{feeble|feeble}} garlic press that has never crushed a clove in its life, and an avocado slicer, which is simply a spoon with ambitions. This week I emptied it. The only thing I kept was a wooden spoon my gran used, its handle worn pale, and a jar of dried rose {{petals|petal}} I keep meaning to put in a cake.

title: Rovers 0, City 5
text: City {{obliterated|obliterate}} Rovers under a {{dense|dense}} fog that made the far goal a rumour for most of the first half. Rovers' back line was {{feeble|feeble}} from the first minute, and by the fourth goal the home fans had stopped singing and started leaving. Their manager, visibly {{irritated|irritate}}, refused to blame the weather. "The fog was the same at both ends," he said. "Only one team could see the ball."

title: First date, Peckham
text: He was {{amiable|amiable}} enough, in the way estate agents are amiable, and for the first hour Priya was polite. Then the second gin arrived and her {{inhibitions|inhibition}} went with the first. She told him about the flat with the {{damp|damp}} bathroom, the ex, the cat that hated her. Nothing could {{dampen|dampen}} the mood after that, not even when he admitted he had never read a book all the way through. She found, to her surprise, that she wanted a third gin.

title: Notice to tenants
text: Dear Resident, following the survey of the {{posterior|posterior}} wall of Block C, the council has agreed that the {{damp|damp}} is structural and not, as previously suggested, caused by residents drying washing indoors. Work begins in June. We are not yet {{at liberty|at liberty}} to confirm the contractor. We understand that some tenants feel a lasting {{enmity|enmity}} towards the housing office after the last two years, and we hope this letter goes some way to repairing that.
